title: Knowledge check: Introduction to Database Integration

questions.prompt: Which subtopic is explicitly listed under “Introduction to Database Integration” in the attached Classic ASP curriculum?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists “Why ASP applications use databases” under lesson 65, “Introduction to Database Integration”. The distractors belong to other lesson topics.

questions.prompt: When applying “Introduction to Database Integration” in a legacy Classic ASP application, which approach is strongest?
options: Concatenate user values directly into SQL.
Return the full connection string to the browser when debugging.
Keep every Recordset open for the whole session.
Validate input, bind values as ADO parameters, and close database resources reliably.
questions.answer_key: Validate input, bind values as ADO parameters, and close database resources reliably.
questions.explanation: This approach keeps introduction to database integration testable and respects Classic ASP/IIS runtime boundaries. The exact IIS, provider, or component behavior must be checked in the target test environment.

questions.prompt: Before marking work on “Introduction to Database Integration” ready for review, what evidence should be recorded?
options: Delete diagnostic evidence before recording the outcome.
Treat a successful happy-path test as proof of all security properties.
Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
Claim the production deployment passed without running it.
questions.answer_key: Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
questions.explanation: Good maintenance evidence includes the expected and observed result, relevant version/runtime assumptions, and a boundary or failure test. Never claim an execution/deployment test that was not run.

notes: Answer keys and explanations are repository-side protected content. The learner API must return prompts/options and only reveal grading feedback after submission.
